name: What is the difference between building out versus building up for an addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between building out versus building up for an addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A ground-floor bump-out expands outward onto your lot, whereas a second-story addition builds directly upward onto existing framing and foundations. Building out is typically simpler to access during construction, but it consumes yard space and requires foundation excavation. Adding a second story preserves outdoor space but demands structural reinforcement of lower-level framing, temporary roof removal, and specialized coordination. At HH Remodeling, our crew handles the custom framing, drywall, and finish carpentry on-site while coordinating licensed specialty trades for structural, plumbing, and electrical requirements.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building out expands onto yard space with new foundation work, while building up adds a second level, requiring structural reinforcement of the existing home.
